sector: A B2B distributor of OEM elevator and electrical replacement components, sold to service technicians, maintenance supervisors and electrical contractors.
founded_place_size: Cleveland, Ohio; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
about: Girdermark Components is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Cleveland, Ohio, and this commission covers phase 2: data-sheet and bin-label library.
audience: Working buyers aged thirty five to sixty who have specified this class of part for twenty years and judge a supplier by whether the picture and the numbers match.
price_positioning: Parts from 400 to 9,000 dollars. A flat, even, technical register: one neutral photographic ground, the whole part in frame, generous spec setting, prices plain in the run of the page. Never bright consumer tool styling and never dark cinematic hero work. The bin label answers to a picker at arm's length, so it is bigger, blunter and carries less.
typography: A technical, legible system: a neutral grotesque sans for part numbers, spec tables and labels where clarity at small size and at arm's length is everything, with a plain companion for running copy. No decorative or humanist warmth. Note that no chosen face can reach the printer's sheet or the label house's label, which keep their existing typography.
voice: Blunt, factual and useful. No marketing adjectives, no styling in the words. Example line the brand would write: "Sixteen active parts this season. Specs, codes and prices are exactly as our system holds them."
brand_assets_status: The division owns none of its own artwork. The spec sheet and the bin label exist only as the flat press PDFs the printer and the label house return. The house mark was lost in an office move and survives only in the printed sheet header and cast into an aluminium nameplate riveted to an old traction machine in the back, photographed for reference. Part photography was shot in house on the bench over several months and does not match.
values: Accuracy above all: the picture and the spec must agree, values are never reworded to fit, and anything that will not fit is raised before it prints.
